headline: No documented interaction pathway; both docs-only open-source profiles show no shared channels, writes, or data flow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Neither profile exposes an input channel from the other: both have io_surfaces empty, network_egress is none, and both are non-runnable docs-only entries. With no shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP surface documented, a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced for either agent.
conditions: IF either profile later documents a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge, reassess upward.
IF one agent begins parsing the other's file or message output as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Disable any future shared clipboard or workspace bridge.
Add provenance checks before consuming external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, both have network_egress set to none, and no shared workspace or authenticated principal is documented. On the current profiles, there is no plausible leakage path from one agent to the other or onward.
conditions: IF either agent is later given a shared workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF either agent gains outbound network access, reassess for exfiltration.
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of any shared directory.
Review future permission changes before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles show empty concurrency_model and no write-capable surfaces, filesystem permissions, or mutable resource scopes. Without documented writes or overlapping mutable targets, there is no capability conflict to analyze for this pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted write access to the same directory or mutable resource, conflict risk becomes plausible.
IF an orchestrator adds shared locking-free state, reassess upward.
mitigations: Introduce locking before any shared mutable resource is added.
Keep the agents read-only in current deployments.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The profiles do not document that one agent consumes the other's outputs, and both are non-runnable docs-only entries with no I/O surfaces. Without an output-to-input chain, there is no evidence of cascading error between awesome-python and taipy.
conditions: IF an orchestrator starts feeding one agent's output directly into the other, reassess.
IF either agent is used as an authoritative source for downstream actions, cascading error becomes plausible.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between outputs and actions.
Log provenance for any future handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both data_classes_touched fields are empty. With only docs-only open-source metadata, there is no compliance mismatch evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF future profiles assign regulated data classes or residency constraints, reassess compliance.
IF either agent is deployed under a policy with retention or DPA requirements, verify those controls separately.
mitigations: Record data residency and retention requirements before use.
Avoid routing regulated data through undocumented components.
Recheck compliance if deployment scope changes.
